lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Correction and reflection: reflecting and setting a next step

standardsRefs: Ready for Life v1, Grade 4 Unit 6: Family Contribution Capstone
Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice reflecting and setting a next step. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: Using your results from checking your contribution in the previous lesson, you now look back across the whole project, choosing, planning, safety-checking, carrying out, and checking, and decide on one specific next step: fixing a partly-met or missed criterion, extending the contribution further, or starting a new one using what you learned.
safetyNotes: If your next step involves a tool, appliance, or cleaning product, note that it will need the same adult check-in as your original plan before you act on it.
Keep your reflection focused on the task and the process, not on sharing private details about yourself or your household.
If setting your next step means re-observing your contribution one more time, only do so in spaces you already have permission to be in.

simulationAlternative.description: If a trusted adult is not available today to confirm the reflection and next step, the learner completes the full written reflection and next-step plan independently and reviews it with that adult at the next available opportunity, earning full credit once the adult confirms it.

materials: learner-local: notes and results from every earlier lesson in this project
learner-local: paper or a notes app for the written reflection

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u06-l06-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u06-l06-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u06-l06-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u06-l06-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Explain what you learned about your own planning or follow-through from doing this whole project, separate from how the contribution itself turned out.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u06-l06-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g4-u06-l06-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g4-u06-l06-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Stage-by-stage reflection specificity: All five earlier stages are covered, each with a specific strength and a specific thing the learner would do differently. | Next-step concreteness and connection to evidence: The next step is specific, connects directly to the weakest criterion or a specific stage note, and includes a rough timeframe. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u06-l06-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner write a one-paragraph plan for how they would teach the same choose-plan-check-reflect process to someone else taking on a household contribution for the first time.

resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Using your results from checking your contribution in the previous lesson, you now look back across the whole project, choosing, planning, safety-checking, carrying out, and checking, and decide on one specific next step: fixing a partly-met or missed criterion, extending the contribution further, or starting a new one using what you learned.

resources.title: reflecting and setting a next step action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal for reflecting and setting a next step.
2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u06-l06-model-card.
3. Do one coached move on swk-rfl-g4-u06-l06-guided-card.
4. Complete the chosen route on swk-rfl-g4-u06-l06-independent-card.
5. Save the small record on swk-rfl-g4-u06-l06-evidence-record; use swk-rfl-g4-u06-l06-retry-pair if a step is missed.

resources.title: reflecting and setting a next step coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Using your results from checking your contribution in the previous lesson, you now look back across the whole project, choosing, planning, safety-checking, carrying out, and checking, and decide on one specific next step: fixing a partly-met or missed criterion, extending the contribution further, or starting a new one using what you learned.
Coach direction: Before writing your reflection, reread your day-five check results.
Learner prompt: Name the one criterion from your check that came out best and the one that came out weakest.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: reflecting and setting a next step complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Walk back through each stage of the project, choosing, planning, safety-checking, carrying out, and checking, and note one specific thing that went well and one specific thing you would do differently at each stage.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I covered all five earlier stages, not just the carrying-out day.
Response 2 (t2-p2): Each note is a specific detail from what actually happened, not a general 'it was fine.'
Response 3 (t2-p3): I identified at least one thing I would genuinely do differently next time.

Equal-access rule: If a trusted adult is not available today to confirm the reflection and next step, the learner completes the full written reflection and next-step plan independently and reviews it with that adult at the next available opportunity, earning full credit once the adult confirms it.

resources.title: reflecting and setting a next step minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain what you learned about your own planning or follow-through from doing this whole project, separate from how the contribution itself turned out.

Success checks: Stage-by-stage reflection specificity: All five earlier stages are covered, each with a specific strength and a specific thing the learner would do differently. | Next-step concreteness and connection to evidence: The next step is specific, connects directly to the weakest criterion or a specific stage note, and includes a rough timeframe.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: reflecting and setting a next step supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g4-u06-l06-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g4-u06-l06-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional reflecting and setting a next step condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Stage-by-stage reflection specificity: All five earlier stages are covered, each with a specific strength and a specific thing the learner would do differently. | Next-step concreteness and connection to evidence: The next step is specific, connects directly to the weakest criterion or a specific stage note, and includes a rough timeframe..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u06-l06-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
